messages:
anya: Heads up — need a quick sync on routing safeguards for model-variant fallbacks. I hit a couple of edge cases where tokenizer mismatches + tool-calling proto differences lead to silent failures (clients get a partial tool payload). Anyone seen this recently?

mike: Can you paste a tiny repro or an example request that fails?

anya: Minimal repro: client triggers an OCR tool call. Variant A (primary) accepts function calling as {\"name\": \"ocr\", \"args\": {...}} while fallback B expects {\"toolInvoke\": \"ocr\", \"params\": {...}}. On top of that, B's tokenizer tokenizes the prompt differently and truncates the tail, chopping the function signature. Result: fallback answers without calling the tool.

srinivas: That sounds like two distinct compatibility classes: tokenizer-tokencount parity and tool-call protocol parity. We should capture both in the compatibility matrix and add a telemetry signal when tool params drop.

olivia: Proposed matrix columns: tokenizer_family, vocab_delta_flag, max_context_tokens, tool_call_proto (function|legacy|none), truncation_mode (head|tail|smart), and safe_fallback boolean. Also a short notes field listing known truncation hotspots (e.g., long filename lists).

kat: We have a small internal table but it's per-model, not per-variant. Routing decisions are per-variant. We need the router to consult variant-level compat metadata. Also consider quota tier — some customers (enterprise) can accept a higher-cost compatible variant as fallback, but free-tier can't.

mike: UX question: in Console rollouts, do we show a \"compat risk\" badge next to canary targets? Ops should quickly see if a target is 'tool-call-unsafe'.

anya: Yes — show a badge + hover tooltip with failing checks. Also block automatic canary rollouts if tool_call_proto mismatch AND the customer has >5% of calls using function-calling. We should fail-fast instead of silently degrading.

carlos: Telemetry idea: emit event `fallback_toolcall_mismatch` with fields model_from, model_to, lost_fields_list, token_delta. Anonymize prompt text but keep token_delta and example request hash for lookup.

srinivas: Router gating heuristics suggestion: allow fallback if (abs(token_delta) <= 5) OR (tool_call_proto matches). Otherwise, prefer regional fallback (same model family in another region) or degrade with an informative 4xx-level response indicating 'incompatible fallback'.

olivia: Also add a \"compat_score\" to the model catalog computed by CI e2e tests (tokenization diffs, toolcall parity, context edgecases). Router picks highest compat_score that meets latency/quota constraints.

mike: Performance concern: computing tokenizer diffs on every routing decision is heavy. Cache per-model tokenization fingerprints keyed by prompt prefix hash. Fingerprint can be first N tokens for typical prompts.

anya: Example of the tool proto mismatch (redacted):
```json
// primary
{"tool_call": {"name": "ocr", "args": "{\"file_url\": \"...\"}"}}
// fallback
{"toolInvoke": "ocr", "params": {"file_url": "..."}}
```
If fallback truncates the last 40 chars, the JSON becomes malformed and model never calls tool.

kat: Next steps I propose: (1) update the planner doc with new matrix columns, (2) implement the `fallback_toolcall_mismatch` telemetry event and a small aggregation job, (3) console badge mockups for compat risk — I'll draft a figma and put a link in the RFC.

anya: I'll open an RFC with the repro + test vectors and add a small e2e that fails onboarding when parity is broken. Also will add the auto-block rule for canaries when function-calling usage >5%.

mike: +1 on RFC. One more thought: in the router config, expose a togglable policy `allow_incompatible_fallbacks` per-customer so platform teams can opt-in for resilience over correctness. Defaults to false.

srinivas: Agree but make it audited and rate-limited. Also surface the decision in logs and the Console change history.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary check job scheduled: compat-e2e/variant-sanity today 18:00 UTC

kat: I'll start the figma + planner updates. tagging @anya to add the repro and @carlos for telemetry schema.

anya: Thanks all — I'll add the RFC link and the failing test vectors once I open it. :thumbsup:

mike: :thumbsup:
